sections.html:
Castle Rock is the Douglas County seat, set where Interstate 25 meets State Highway 86. Downtown Denver is 28 miles north and Colorado Springs is 37 miles south. At 6,224 feet, it sits higher than most Front Range suburbs.

Growth has been rapid. The town went from 48,231 residents in 2010 to 73,158 in the 2020 census, a jump of 51.68 percent, and the 2025 estimate is 83,815. Median household income for 2019 to 2023 was $145,197, and the median owner-occupied home was worth $652,900 for 2020 to 2024. Single-family permits peaked at 1,169 in 2021 and slowed to about 685 in 2023, so new construction offers a little less competition than it did a few years ago.

About 80 percent of residents leave town for work, and the town has little land zoned for industry. Health care, education and social assistance form the largest industry group at 16.1 percent, followed by professional, scientific and management services at 10.3 percent and finance, insurance and real estate at 9.7 percent. AdventHealth Castle Rock is the only hospital.

With so many people driving to Denver or Colorado Springs each day, a new job or a transfer can force a quick move. That is a common reason owners here want a sale on a short, predictable schedule.

Castle Rock is arranged around I-25 and U.S. 87, which share a north-south path through town. Exit 184 is where U.S. 85 joins I-25, and State Highway 86 comes in from the east and turns into Founders Parkway. Voters left the Regional Transportation District in November 2005, so there is no RTD bus or light rail to Denver. The town does offer a reduced-fare taxi voucher program and a senior center shuttle. Freight trains on the BNSF and Union Pacific lines run alongside U.S. 85.

Buyers who commute care about how long the drive takes and how much road or train noise reaches the yard. Buyers ask about commute and noise, so be ready to describe how close your street is to the highway or the tracks.

Statements go out each January to the owner of record on the tax roll. The county bills owners, not mortgage lenders, and a statement that never arrived does not excuse a late payment. If a lender collects your taxes through escrow, check that the account is actually paying them. More is on the Douglas County tax dates page.

sections.h2: Snow, sun and wear on the house
sections.html:
Winters are cold, dry and snowy, and summers are hot and wetter, with August bringing the most rain. January runs about 45.6 degrees for the average high and 18.0 for the low, while July's average high is 85.7. Records span from 102 degrees in July to 37 below zero in January. Yearly totals average 17.60 inches of precipitation and 57.5 inches of snow.

Roofs, gutters, decks and driveways carry that load. When a buyer's inspector writes up those items, the price can slip or the deal can stall, which is one reason owners with tired exteriors look at a sale to a buyer who accepts the house as it stands.

The Douglas County School District is based in Castle Rock and runs 18 public schools in town, including Castle View High School and Douglas County High School. Attendance follows the address, so send a buyer to the district if they want to confirm an assignment. Do not promise a particular school yourself, since boundaries can change.

A tax balance will not stop a sale, but it must be cleared before the buyer receives clean title. Closing staff request the current figure from the county, list it on the settlement statement and deduct it from what you receive. Learn the number early so the table holds no surprises.

Two small cautions apply. First, the due dates move when they land on a weekend, so a payment you planned for the last day of February may be owed on the next business day. Second, a statement addressed to a prior owner can sit unopened for months, so verify that the county has your name and mailing address before you list.

Listing a clean house in a willing market can fetch more money. It also brings open houses, an inspection, repair requests and a wait for the buyer's financing. A cash bid gives up part of that price in return for certainty and speed. For a house with an old roof, worn decks or a yard that needs work, the gap between the two numbers is often smaller than owners expect once repairs and carrying time are counted.

Get every offer on paper, with the closing date and cost split spelled out, and lay them next to each other before replying to anyone. A serious buyer will not mind the request, and it protects you if the terms change later.

sections.h2: What Castle Rock sellers tend to face
sections.html:
Many sellers need speed, or own a house that has aged. Typical cases:

  • a job move with a date set by an employer
  • a house left to heirs who have no wish to keep it up
  • roof, deck or landscaping wear after snowy winters and drought rules
  • an owner tired of the idea of showings and negotiation

A cash buyer means no lender and no appraisal. What you owe on the property stays the same, though, so get payoff and tax numbers from the title company before you agree to anything.

sections.h2: How a Castle Rock cash sale runs
sections.html:
Title and recording work proceeds just as it would for a mortgage buyer. The only thing that vanishes is lender underwriting.

  1. Give us the address and tell us what shape the house is in.
  2. We send a written offer for the house as it is.
  3. A title company checks taxes and liens on the Douglas County parcel.
  4. You close, and the deed is recorded in Douglas County.

If the numbers do not suit you, you can walk away with no obligation. Before you decide, line the offer up against what a listing might net after repairs, agent costs and the months of waiting.

A few papers speed things along: the current tax statement, any mortgage payoff information, and the names of everyone on the deed. If your lender pays taxes through escrow, bring that statement too, so the title company can confirm what has been paid.

faqs.q: What county is Castle Rock, CO in?
faqs.a: Castle Rock is in Douglas County and is its county seat.

faqs.q: When is the full property tax payment due in Castle Rock?
faqs.a: April 30 under Douglas County's schedule. Half payments are due the last day of February and June 15.

faqs.q: Is there RTD service from Castle Rock to Denver?
faqs.a: No. Castle Rock voters left the Regional Transportation District in November 2005, so there is no RTD bus or light rail service to Denver.

faqs.q: Who receives the property tax statement?
faqs.a: Statements go each January to the owner of record on the tax roll. The county does not bill mortgage lenders, so confirm that any escrow account is paying the tax.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Castle Rock house without fixing it up?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as is, so you do not need to repair the roof, yard or interior first. Get the offer in writing and compare it with a listing.
